title: Patch urgency routing and RBAC sync playbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working playbook for routing vulnerability scanner outputs into an urgency-driven remediation pipeline while keeping RBAC v2 role syncs and audit-log exports aligned for SIEM ingestion. Aim: reduce patch-to-verify median time by 40% for P1/P2 classes without adding manual toil to engineering teams. This doc combines the practical routing rules, the RBAC sync considerations (so evidence and ownership are consistent), and the audit/log schema mappings required for SIEM and automated evidence retention.

Background notes (quick):
- Over last two quarters our scanner flood for large infra components spikes during dependency-batch updates; triage latency increases because ownership info is stale in the scanner output (role mappings from legacy directory).
- RBAC v2 rollout means roles are now group-based and dynamic; scanner/evidence systems need to consume role snapshots or a reliable owner attribute.
- SIEM export currently pulls raw scanner JSON -> normalized table, but missing severity-derived routing fields and evidence URIs required for automated patch workflows.

Goals:
1) Define a minimal, implementable pipeline so scanner findings with severity/asset tags are routed to the correct on-call/team slack channel and ticket queue automatically.
2) Ensure RBAC v2 sync process updates the vuln-processing index so findings contain canonical owner/team data at time of ingestion.
3) Produce an audit-log schema and SIEM mapping that preserves actionability (who, when, what evidence) and supports SLA reporting and post-mortem reconstruction.
4) Add lightweight evidence automation: attach build/dep manifests, package manager metadata, and patch links to tickets.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: internal infra + dedicated customer-facing hosts + repo dependency scan outputs.
- Non-goal: full remediation automation (we will not attempt automatic patch pushes).

Roles and responsibilities (short):
- Security Ops: owns the routing rules, SIEM export transforms, and SLA monitoring.
- Platform Eng: provides role directory/role-lookup API (RBAC v2 snapshot endpoint) and on-call channel mapping.
- SRE/Infra teams: own remediation execution; must ensure runbooks exist.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success: for dedicated/private customers, confirm any alternate RBAC mapping required for tenant-isolated assets.

Design overview (high level):
1) Ingest: scanner outputs (OSS scanner + dependency-scan + container-scan) land in vuln-queue-service with raw JSON preserved.
2) Enrich: call RBAC v2 snapshot API for affected asset (by asset-tag or hostname). Add fields: canonical_team, canonical_owner_email, owner_role_version.
3) Prioritize: compute urgency_score = severity_weight * exposure_multiplier * age_factor. If urgency_score >= threshold -> immediate P1/P2 routing.
4) Route: push to ticketing with queue based on canonical_team; send alert to mapped on-call Slack channel and create SIEM event with audit schema.
5) Evidence: attach evidence bundle URL generated by evidence-service (contains scanner output, package manifests, repo link, and recommended patch links).

RBAC v2 sync requirements (practical):
- Snapshots: RBAC service must support point-in-time snapshots for the asset lookup call. When enrichment occurs, include snapshot_id so we can tie a finding to the state of roles when it was processed. This is essential for audits and rollback of ownership if role mappings change.
- Rate limits / cache: caching allowed for 5 minutes for repeated lookups per asset to avoid thundering; stale-cache window must be recorded in enrichment metadata (owner_role_version + cache_ttl_used).
- Fallback: if RBAC query fails, fallback to legacy-owner-key in scanner metadata or tag as "team-unknown" and route to security on-call with higher friction SLA.
- Sync cadence: RBAC publishes delta streams; security pipeline subscribes to delta feed so we can preemptively update canonical_team for frequently scanned assets.

SLA and routing tiers (proposed):
- P1 (critical exploit, public exploit exists, high exposure): 4-hour ack, 48-hour remediation target. Route: canonical_team + security-led war-room + SRE escalation.
- P2 (high severity, internal exploit potential): 8-hour ack, 7-day remediation target. Route: canonical_team, on-call.
- P3 (medium): 3 business-day ack, 30-day remediation.
- P4 (low/info): best-effort, weekly digest.
Notes: ack = ticket created + owner acknowledged. Remediation target measured as time-to-verify (patch applied and scan shows fix).

Audit-log schema (fields we must export to SIEM):
- event_id (uuid)
- event_type (finding_ingested | finding_enriched | ticket_created | evidence_attached | owner_acknowledged | remediation_verified)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- scanner_name (string)
- scanner_finding_id (string)
- asset_id (string)
- asset_tags (comma-separated list)
- canonical_team (string)
- canonical_owner_email (string)
- owner_role_version (string)
- severity (cvss_v3 or custom: critical/high/medium/low)
- urgency_score (numeric string)
- routing_queue (string)
- ticket_id (string)
- evidence_url (https)
- action (string)
- actor (service name or human email)
- prior_state_snapshot_id (string)
- processing_latency_ms (string)
- retention_policy_tag (string)
- encrypt_flag (true/false as string)
- source_pipeline_version (string)
Comments: all fields must be strings to simplify SIEM ingestion. For numeric measurements we use numeric strings. The audit record should be idempotent and include snapshot ids to allow audit replay.

SIEM export mapping notes (practical):
- Normalize severity: map scanner-specific severities to our canonical set at ingest time. Export both original and normalized values.
- Evidence pointers only: do not export raw scanner output to SIEM index (size/cost). Instead export evidence_url which is an encrypted signed link with 7-day default TTL. SIEM can follow link if the analyst needs full output.
- Tagging: apply "sensitive" flag on evidence_url when artifact contains PII or keys. That should trigger retention_policy_tag = "sensitive-30d".

Evidence automation rules (examples):
- For dependency scanners: attach the repo URL + commit sha + package.json/yarn.lock file snippet and identify known patch PR (if exists in GH) using dependency-PR-matcher service. If no PR exists, craft suggested bump PR template and attach to ticket as draft.
- For container scans: provide image digest + base-image layer CVE list. Provide link to build pipeline that produced offending image (if available) and suggested base image versions.
- For infra host findings: attach apt/yum manifest, kernel version, and recommended CVE fix link. If remediation requires config change, add a remediation-playbook-id to the ticket (short reference).

Ticket schema (what we create in Jira/Ticketing):
- summary: short human readable (max 120 chars)
- description: includes scanner excerpt, evidence_url, reproducible steps if available
- labels: vuln, scanner_name, severity, canonical_team
- components: canonical_team
- sla_priority: P1/P2/P3/P4
- attachments: evidence_url and precomputed patch PR link when applicable

Edge cases and anti-patterns to avoid:
- Do not rely on email-only ownership from scans. Emails rotate and can be stale. Use canonical_team + on-call rota as primary routing keys.
- Avoid auto-closing tickets based solely on diffed scan results; require explicit remediation verification event.
- For infra spanning multiple teams (e.g., infra service + tenant config), route to both with a primary owner field and secondary-notify list.

Implementation plan (phased):
Phase 0 (2 weeks): add RBAC snapshot call to enrichment pipeline, export snapshot_id in audit logs, and implement fallback routing to security-oncall.
Phase 1 (4 weeks): implement urgency_score, basic routing (Slack + ticket creation), evidence-url generation with TTL 7 days, and SIEM audit schema export for finding_enriched and ticket_created events.
Phase 2 (6 weeks): hook dependency-PR-matcher to attach recommended PRs, add signed evidence URLs with sensitivity flags, and implement SLA dashboards in Console.
Phase 3 (ongoing): iterate thresholds, reduce false positives, and expand to private-deploy customers with tenant-aware routing.

Operational metrics to track (KPIs):
- median_time_to_ack_by_priority (target P1 < 4h)
- median_time_to_verify_by_priority (target P1 < 48h)
- ratio_of_findings_with_canonical_owner (target > 95%)
- evidence_url_follow_rate (how often analysts fetch full bundle)
- false_routing_rate (tickets routed to wrong team confirmed on triage)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should evidence_url TTL be 7 days by default or 30 days behind a retention policy? (privacy vs analyst convenience).
- For private deployments, do we mirror RBAC snapshots to customer-managed stores or call back to customer directory? Legal/privacy implications to confirm.
- SLA exceptions: business-critical infra may need extended remediation windows; how to represent that in routing and audit logs?

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Asha] finalize the canonical field list and publish to Confluence. (SEC-487)
- [Miguel] prototype RBAC snapshot lookup and return format; share example payload by 2026-06-22.
- [Lena] update SIEM mapping with proposed audit-log schema and prototype ingest in dev SIEM.
- [Ben] wire basic Slack routing for P1/P2 with retry/backoff and post messages to #sec-ops-oncall.
- [Priya] create PR template for dependency bump suggestions and integrate with evidence-service.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but pragmatic: keep the first iteration small. Implementation teams should avoid building heavy stateful orchestration in the scanner — use enrichment and evidence-service for attachments and keep the ingest pipeline idempotent.
- If you are an owner of a specific asset group and want a non-standard routing queue, add a short justification in the Confluence page linked above.

End of playbook (working doc).
